**Observation Log:**

- [TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/08/30 (Wed) 05:56
- [USER] User inquired about the content of an article regarding AI regulation.
- [USER] User referenced the "General Data Protection Regulation" from Wikipedia.
- [FACT] GDPR is a European Union regulation on data protection and privacy in the EU and the European Economic Area (EEA).
- [FACT] GDPR was adopted on 14 April 2016 and became enforceable beginning 25 May 2018.
- [FACT] GDPR supersedes the Data Protection Directive 95/46/EC.
- [FACT] GDPR applies to any enterprise processing personal information of individuals inside the EEA, regardless of the enterprise's location.
- [FACT] GDPR aims to enhance individuals' control and rights over their personal data and simplify the regulatory environment for international business.
- [FACT] GDPR is directly binding and applicable, allowing flexibility for individual member states to adjust certain aspects.
- [FACT] GDPR has influenced laws in countries such as Turkey, Mauritius, Chile, Japan, Brazil, South Korea, South Africa, Argentina, and Kenya.
- [FACT] As of 6 October 2022, the UK retains GDPR in identical form despite no longer being an EU member state.
- [FACT] The California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) has many similarities with the GDPR.
- [FACT] GDPR consists of eleven chapters covering various aspects of data protection.
- [FACT] The regulation applies if the data controller, processor, or data subject is based in the EU.
- [FACT] GDPR does not apply to personal data processing for purely personal or household activities.
- [FACT] Personal data is defined as information relating to an identified or identifiable individual.
- [FACT] GDPR includes provisions for the processing of personal data for national security activities or law enforcement.
- [FACT] Each EU member state establishes an independent supervisory authority (SA) to handle complaints and sanctions.
- [FACT] A European Data Protection Board (EDPB) coordinates the SAs across member states.
- [FACT] GDPR introduced a risk-based approach to data protection enforcement.
- [FACT] The risk-based approach requires data controllers to evaluate risks at each stage of the data life cycle.
- [FACT] Personal data processing requires at least one legal basis as outlined in Article 6 of GDPR.
- [FACT] Consent must be explicit, specific, and freely given for data processing.
- [FACT] Data subjects can withdraw consent at any time, and the process must be easy.
- [FACT] Consent for children under 16 must be given by a parent or custodian.
- [FACT] Article 12 requires data controllers to provide information to data subjects in a clear and accessible manner.
- [FACT] Article 15 grants data subjects the right to access their personal data and information about its processing.
